items.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025
items.q: Benny Goodman and Pete Fountain are my heroes... I’ve read everything I could on him and read it a hundred times over

ctx.x: Do you think — you might not be able to answer this because you’re not other jazz musicians, but do you feel that you pay more attention to the audience when you’re improvising than the typical jazz musician who may be playing more for themselves?

That’s a good question. I don’t know if I can compare myself in that mindset to other people because I don’t know what they’re thinking necessarily, but I know that for me personally I can feel the vibe of a crowd very quickly, you know whether they’re with us or not. I mean my own personal taste, I don’t really go for jazz that’s really far out. That’s just me. I mean as far as jazz goes I’m really drawn to swing and you know, Benny Goodman and Pete Fountain are my heroes and obviously a lot of the guys that…

the fifties thing. So it was a little harder, there was more ice to cut through then, so I just didn’t do it as much for those crowds frankly. But now everybody seems to just enjoy a good song you know.

items.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025
items.q: I remember Dan Barrett telling me that when he was in Benny’s last big band... from my mind as far as being a clarinet player I don’t think anybody played like him prior to him.

ctx.x: I remember Dan Barrett telling me that when he was in Benny’s last big band, that Benny would rehearse the band without the rhythm section you know. And he didn’t want to hear any toes tapping either. You know like they had to have such an internal sense of swing and rhythm, and he said it was really scary because he was watching them and listening. But he understood what he was driving at and it was very effective. The band really learned how to drive forward and I thought that’s — you know because Benny’s gift…
You studied his career — why do you think he was dubbed “The King of Swing?”

Boy. Well from my mind as far as being a clarinet player I don’t think anybody played like him prior to him. You know that’s number one. And I think he came along just at a time where that whole thing was meant to be. You know I mean he just had such an incredible band and it swung harder — in my estimation it swung harder than anybody else. That’s just my opinion. It was tight, it was musically pristine yet loose, and it drove really hard. And I don’t know it was just a winning formula. It was just probably by…
